angle_name: Reciprocal min-splice PNT bound + involution-closure lemma (ADJACENT ANGLE — honest verdict: pure sign-preserving summation calculus cannot touch rung 2)
mechanism: Honest core claim first: Abel summation, the hyperbola/reciprocal swap, Euler–Maclaurin, and smooth reweighting form an involutive calculus on S = Σ_{d≤K} μ(d)R(⌊x/d⌋); at the self-dual point y ≍ √x every composite of these moves returns a conjugate of S itself (the repo has already kernel-proved the two faces equal in PrimeSieveAbelIdentity.lean), so rearrangement alone conserves the information and can never manufacture the rung-2 estimate. What the lens CAN deliver is a quantitative sign-aware bound using both faces simultaneously. Split d into dyadic blocks [D,2D) with D ≤ K. On the d-side face, every argument satisfies x/d ≥ y ≍ √x, so the unconditional PNT error (de la Vallee Poussin exp(−c√log t), or Vinogradov–Korobov exp(−c(log t)^{3/5}(loglog t)^{−1/5}) on paper) applies uniformly at long range: Σ_{d∈[D,2D)} |R(⌊x/d⌋)| ≪ x·exp(−c(log(x/D))^{3/5−ε}). On the Mertens face (the kernel-proved reciprocal form), the same block is Σ_{m∈[D,2D)} M(m)·(interval discrepancy), bounded by max_{m∼D}|M(m)| times the interval prime mass ≪ D·exp(−c(log D)^{3/5−ε})·(x/D)/log(x/D). Take the minimum face per block and sum over ≍ log x blocks: unconditionally |S| ≪ x (log x) exp(−c'(log x)^{3/5−ε}), a genuine PNT-strength o(x) bound — rung 0 — with no RH input anywhere, including the d=1 term R(x) and the boundary M(K)R(y). The structural payoff is a recalibration of the ladder: the packet's "triangle-inequality scale ≈ x^{3/4}" is a finite-range artifact of R behaving like √t empirically; the honest unconditional trivial scale is x log x exp(−c(log x)^{3/5−ε}), so rung 1 (any power saving x^{1−δ}) is far above every known unconditional tool. Indeed via Perron, S ≈ Σ_ρ P(ρ)x^ρ/ρ with P(s) = Σ_{d≤K}μ(d)d^{−s} a truncation of 1/ζ; a hypothetical zero β₀ near 1 makes P(ρ₀) resonate (truncated 1/ζ at its own singularity, trivially only ≪ K^{1−β₀}/(1−β₀)), and the K = √x truncation converts a zero's contribution to size x^{(1+β₀)/2} — so an unconditional rung-1 bound would demand exactly the zero-free-strip-strength control nobody has; I assess rung 1 as quasi-strip-hard, and rung 2 as requiring input strictly outside summation calculus (bilinear/spectral/zero-density valid at the pinned x). All capability claims here about what is available in mathlib/the repo beyond the files I read are UNVERIFIED.
new_leverage: Using BOTH kernel-proved faces of the same identity simultaneously as a per-dyadic-block min-envelope (μ-side long-range PNT error vs Mertens-side M(m)=o(m)), rather than either face alone; plus the involution-closure observation itself, which is new negative leverage: it extends the F-closure audit to the entire orbit of summation-calculus rearrangements and recalibrates the strength ladder unconditionally (honest trivial scale x·log x·exp(−c(log x)^{3/5−ε}), not x^{3/4}). Nothing here is a new inequality; the leverage is exact bookkeeping already half-formalized in PrimeSieveAbelIdentity.lean plus classical unconditional inputs.
target_estimate: Reciprocal min-splice PNT bound: for x ≥ x₀, y = ⌊√x⌋, K = ⌊x/(y+1)⌋, unconditionally |Σ_{d=1}^{K} μ(d)(π(⌊x/d⌋) − Li(⌊x/d⌋))| ≤ C·x·(log x)·exp(−c(log x)^{3/5}(log log x)^{−1/5}) (paper strength; exponent degrades to 1/2 with only de la Vallee Poussin, and to whatever error term is actually formalized if done in Lean — UNVERIFIED what that is). Variables and losses: dyadic blocks D = 2^j ≤ K contribute min[C₁x·exp(−c₁(log(x/D))^{3/5−ε}), C₂(x/log(x/D))·exp(−c₂(log D)^{3/5−ε})]; the log x factor is the block count; the constant in c' degrades by 2^{−3/5} from the self-dual corner D ≍ √x, which dominates. This is rung 0 only; no power saving is claimed and none is achievable by this mechanism.

obstacle_positions.F_closure: Not escaped — endorsed and extended. My mechanism never invokes Σ M(d)^2 nor any Cauchy–Schwarz/Holder recombination; at rung 0 the recombination is exact identity + triangle inequality, which is legitimate at that rung. The extension I claim: the F-closure is stable under the full orbit of Abel/hyperbola/Euler–Maclaurin/smoothing moves because that calculus is involutive on the self-dual sum (both faces already kernel-equal in PrimeSieveAbelIdentity.lean); therefore exiting F requires non-summation input, not cleverer rearrangement.
obstacle_positions.fiber_growth: Untouched. No off-diagonal pair-to-modulus transfer, no reduced denominators, no conductors appear anywhere in the mechanism.
obstacle_positions.pinned_vs_averaged: Immune by construction: every input (dlVP/VK PNT error, unconditional Mertens o-bound) is a pointwise bound valid at the deterministic pinned x; no L^2-averaged translation estimate is used, so no exceptional set can contain x. The price of this immunity is exactly why savings cap at exp(−(log x)^{3/5}): pointwise unconditional inputs go no further.
obstacle_positions.modulus_magnitude: Not engaged. No wheel modulus, no packet-conductor object enters; the mechanism lives entirely in the d/m reciprocal coordinates of the kernel-proved identity.
obstacle_positions.parity: μ enters linearly and is bounded through zero-free-region facts about 1/ζ (Mertens-type bounds), not through sieve weights, so the classical parity wall is not confronted head-on; it manifests instead as the hard cap at exponential-in-(log)^{3/5} savings. I explicitly claim crossing to power savings requires zero-density/spectral input outside this lens.
obstacle_positions.circularity: Clean. The d=1 term R(x) and the boundary M(K)R(y) are bounded only by unconditional PNT error terms (dlVP/VK); no pointwise RH-strength bound is used anywhere, inductively or otherwise. The rung-1 hardness assessment (quasi-zero-free-strip) is stated as an obstruction, not used as an assumption.
obstacle_positions.finite_range: Respected and weaponized: my deliverable is an unconditional theorem, with numerics used only as falsifiers (identity residual checks, constant sanity at x ≤ 10^9), never as support. I additionally flag that the packet's own rung-1 calibration ('triangle scale ≈ x^{3/4} empirically') is itself a finite-range artifact — unconditionally the honest trivial scale is x log x exp(−c(log x)^{3/5−ε}), and the ladder should be restated against that.

kill_test: Two cheap kills, in order. (1) Triviality kill (hours): search literature/repo results for an existing unconditional o(x) or better bound on Σ_{d≤√x}μ(d)R(x/d) — if triangle+PNT is already recorded as known/trivial by the packet authors, the rung-0 deliverable is hollow and only the involution-closure lemma survives; separately, any published unconditional power-saving bound on this sum would kill my 'rung 1 is quasi-strip-hard' thesis outright. (2) Formalization-input kill (one grep session): check whether mathlib or the repo actually contains a quantitative PNT error term strong enough to instantiate the bound (UNVERIFIED); if only Chebyshev-strength or bare o(x) PNT is available, the Lean-facing version of rung 0 dies at bounded effort and only the paper version stands. Numeric sanity (minutes, falsifier only): evaluate both faces and the min-splice envelope at x = 10^6..10^8 and confirm the envelope dominates |S|; failure kills the constant bookkeeping.

Secondary formalizable partial: 'Involution-closure lemma' — every composite of the repo's summation moves (Abel step, reciprocal swap, boundary re-clip) applied to primeSievePNTError yields a form whose triangle envelope is no smaller than the min of the two existing faces; finite algebra over already-proved identities, extending the F-closure audit to the whole summation-calculus orbit.
self_assessed_risk: High, stated plainly. Weakest assumption: that dlVP/VK-strength PNT error terms are available in usable (and for Lean, importable) form — UNVERIFIED, and the entire formalized rung 0 rests on it. Second weakness: the involution-closure claim is an audit-style structural argument, demonstrated on every rearrangement I tried and consistent with the repo's kernel-proved equivalence, but not proved as a general theorem about all summation-calculus moves. Third: insiders may regard triangle+PNT as trivially known, reducing my contribution to the ladder recalibration and the closure lemma. I assess probability near zero that this lens reaches rung 2 by any refinement; probability low that rung 1 is reachable without zero-free-strip-strength input; probability moderate-to-high that the rung-0 theorem plus closure lemma are real, small, durable contributions.
